applies_why: The judge text gives an UNDERDETERMINED verdict for D5 and relies on the matter cutting both ways, which is the kind of two-sense/openness reasoning K-S2 governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: Phrase: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. Readings weighed: (1) a cuts-both-ways or two-sense showing cannot ground UNDERDETERMINED because both senses stand; (2) it leaves D5 open and supports UNDERDETERMINED.
why: The judge makes the almah/bethulah word-count cutting both ways and the coexistence of the chapter bounds with Matthew's application a reason for UNDERDETERMINED, but K-S2 says a verse carrying two senses is not open and both senses stand.
